summary: Iter256 — subscription-enforcement (access_state: active|trial|view_only) verified end-to-end on shared backend + web + mobile. Backend pytest suite (13 tests) 12/13 pass; the single failure is an unrelated route-level 409 no_household gate on GET /api/documents for the view_only fixture (not a subscription-middleware issue). ALL access-state assertions PASS: (1) /api/auth/me returns canonical access_state='active' for cathy, 'trial' for trialactive, 'view_only' for cancelled.vo and trial30909. (2) View-only writes correctly return 402 read_only with the exact 'Your plan is inactive. Reactivate to add or change anything.' copy on POST /api/provider-ratings, POST /api/documents, POST /api/v2/participants. (3) View-only user is NOT blocked on POST /api/payments/checkout (reactivation stays open). (4) Active (cathy) and Trial (trialactive) writes are NOT hit by the read_only middleware (route-level responses only). WEB (viewport 1440x900): logging in as cancelled.vo@example.com pins the ReadOnlyBanner (data-testid='read-only-banner') at top of /app with the exact copy and Reactivate CTA; /settings/billing reachable with plan cards + Reactivate button; cathy and trialactive show NO banner post-login. MOBILE (viewport 390x844, Expo web preview): logging in as cancelled.vo@example.com renders the ViewOnlyBanner (testID='view-only-banner') pinned at top with the same copy + Reactivate button (testID='view-only-banner-reactivate'); tapping Reactivate navigates to /plan-billing which shows the 'No active plan / Start your free trial' CTA. cathy and trialactive show NO view-only banner on mobile.

minor.issue: Returns 409 no_household for cancelled.vo@example.com (view_only fixture has no household). Not a subscription-enforcement bug — the middleware correctly does NOT fire on GETs — but the fixture cannot exercise the 'GET returns 200' assertion for /api/documents. Either seed a household on cancelled.vo, or pick a different GET endpoint for the view_only 200 assertion.

action_items: (INFO) Seed a household on cancelled.vo@example.com (or swap the GET-returns-200 assertion to a household-agnostic endpoint like /api/v2/participants which already passes) so the pytest file is fully green without env drift.

(INFO for E1) Trial-end auto-charge via Stripe (subscription+trial+saved-card) is native Stripe behaviour and was NOT exercised in preview per request; the DB gating, /auth/me access_state, the read_only middleware, and the reactivation carve-out are all working.
critical_code_review_comments: _compute_access_state (server.py L2929) correctly handles stale 'trialing' status: guards trial_ends_at <= now → view_only. Verified fixture trial30909@example.com resolves to view_only despite subscription_status='trialing'.

_enforce_read_only_for_unpaid middleware (server.py L7477) exempts /api/payments/, /api/billing/, /api/auth/, /api/webhook/stripe, /api/stripe/, /api/users/me, /api/admin/, /api/health, /api/metrics, /api/public/. Note: /api/support/tickets was intentionally removed from the exempt tuple (L7471-7473) — spec says view-only users cannot open support tickets. Confirm this matches product intent (view-only user can NOT create a support ticket).

Middleware short-circuits view_only writes with 402 body {detail:{error:'trial_expired', read_only:true, upgrade_url:'/settings/billing', message:'Your plan is inactive. Reactivate to add or change anything.'}} — matches web ReadOnlyBanner copy and mobile ViewOnlyBanner copy exactly.
Admin bypass verified via _compute_access_state guard 'if user.get(is_admin): return active' — admins never see view_only regardless of subscription state.

success_rate.backend: 92% (12/13 — the 1 miss is a fixture-data issue, not the middleware)
success_rate.frontend: 100% for the flows under review — web + mobile view-only banner, copy, Reactivate CTA, and active/trial no-banner all verified

seed_data_creation: None. Used the four fixture accounts documented in /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_access_state_enforcement_iter256.py is the canonical regression suite for the three-state access model. Run via `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest backend/tests/test_access_state_enforcement_iter256.py -v`. Web selectors: data-testid='read-only-banner' + [data-testid*='read-only-lock']. Mobile selectors: testID='view-only-banner' + testID='view-only-banner-reactivate'. The banner mounts inside the authenticated app shell only (marketing 404 pages will not show it — expected). The full Stripe trial-end auto-charge → view-only flip loop requires a real webhook and cannot be smoke-tested in the preview env; verify DB flip + /auth/me access_state via a direct mongo update to simulate the webhook (subscription.status: canceled | past_due | expired) if a live end-to-end is needed later.
rca of the issue: No regressions. Only cosmetic finding: pytest assertion for GET /api/documents returning 200 for view_only user fails because that fixture has no household (returns 409 no_household). The subscription middleware itself is correct — the failure is fixture data. Fix by either seeding a household on cancelled.vo@example.com or switching the assertion to /api/v2/participants (which already passes 200 for view_only).
